outcome.technical: MED 1: _output.py gains a section `what a refused kernel lock call means`: LOCK_HELD/LOCK_REFUSED/LOCK_FAILED, LOCK_HELD_ERRNOS (moved from _locks), LOCK_REFUSED_ERRNOS = {ENOLCK, EOPNOTSUPP, ENOTSUP, ENOSYS} where defined, and kernel_lock_refusal(exc, msvcrt_call=False), which reads EINVAL as refused only when msvcrt_call is set; everything else is LOCK_FAILED. _locks.py keeps only LOCK_TAKEN; _try_lock passes msvcrt_call=(fcntl is None); _dir_mutex tracks seen_held, degrades only on LOCK_REFUSED with no held answer earlier in the same wait, and otherwise raises _lock_call_failed(mutex, mode, exc, seen_held), which keeps the call's errno and names the descriptor mode (read-only EBADF names the NFS byte-range cause; the case where the mutex was seen held says so). _open_mutex now returns (fd, mode). _claim/_take_over/_remove_claim catch that OSError into the error answer as before (sharing_denied is EACCES only, and EACCES is always read as held, so it never reaches the raise). LOW 2: usage_ledger no longer imports _locks; lock_month asks _output.kernel_lock_refusal(exc, msvcrt_call=msvcrt is not None) != LOCK_HELD, so anything not held, a failed call included, stays lock-free as before. Docs: SECURITY.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md now name the explicit set and the error cases, and the guide's module map no longer shows the usage_ledger -> _locks edge. Tests: test__locks.py adds mx18-mx22 (helpers _SequencedFlock, _RefusingMsvcrt, _mx_enter, _mx_claim_with, _mx_errno_cases); test_usage_ledger.py rewrites lf7 against _output (EIO added: expected unavailable; the swapped reading is now always-held -> all None) and adds lf8 (a fresh interpreter imports usage_ledger; sys.modules holds _output and usage_ledger and no _locks). Results: test__locks 189 cases, test_usage_ledger 140 cases, test__output 91 cases, all ok; a 46-file sweep (every tests/test_*.py naming _locks or usage_ledger, plus test_audit_usage, test__output_lints, test__deps, test__output, tools/measure-context.py) exit 0, 46/46 files ok; bench-hooks --gate exit 0, measured once on 3.14.7 only (3.8-3.13 not measured, as the tool prints). Not verified: that the Windows CRT reports an unsupported volume lock as EINVAL. That is the task's premise and the CRT's default _dosmaperr mapping, and it was not run on Windows. Dependants: _evidence_io, _invariants, _proc_group, audit-lock, drive-phase, stamp-verification, _proposals and audit-task still hold, because none of them names kernel_lock_refusal, LOCK_HELD, LOCK_REFUSED or _HELD_ERRNOS (grep across plugins/tools/.claude/hooks finds no hits outside the declared files) and _claim's answer shape is unchanged. tests/test_audit_lock.py, test_audit_task.py and test_run_test_gate.py are green in the sweep. usage_ledger's dependants (meter-usage hook, _invariants, commit-task-work, _panel_page, _panel_viewer, _usage_load, audit-status, audit-usage) are green in the sweep; the ledger's public names are unchanged and it now loads one module fewer. _output's dependants: additions only, no name changed, test__output_lints, test__deps and test__output green. SECURITY.md and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md readers: changed prose only, and the prose lints are green. No file outside the declared set was edited; the docs/audit journal and phase-file changes in the tree are the orchestrator's.
outcome.descriptive: Only ENOLCK/EOPNOTSUPP/ENOTSUP/ENOSYS (and msvcrt EINVAL) skip the claim mutex now; every other lock errno, and a refusal after a held answer, is an error naming the descriptor mode, and the ledger reads the shared errno set from _output without loading _locks on the hook path.
